reason: The row-local review closes Slater only for defect detection: ghost-row witnesses 'vanish on the row-sum ideal R', so they cannot see defects lying in R. That is one structural remark about one use. The same vanishing on R makes these simplex functionals (which span (A/R)^*, thm:multirow-local-spanning) exactly the raw material of a Nullstellensatz design, and the bridge's overlap formula gives their values on clause tops. A1's certificate half still needs such a design.
open_statement: A1 (certificate half: Nullstellensatz/local design on a dense block's allowed set)
next_attempt: Use lem:ghost-slater-pairing to write the vanishing of a combination of simplex functionals on one dense block's clause multiples as a bordered-minor (Gram-type) linear system, and test its rank on the recorded dense obstructions (tensor family c=2, seed-23 pair) for a local design.

reason: The equivalence review records it as Developed: in the column representation the defect disappears and the detecting direction is r_i. The generic-core review then closes its last form, the rank-variety weakening, because the single-direction obstructions carry genuine falls (prop:varying-shift-affine-fall, proved for every board with m>=2). The graded form of Dade continues in entry-2026-09-27-graded-dade, so the idea is not lost.

The bridge's one recommendation, to look at second-order data, targeted the U-shifted defect. The equivalence review found that this defect was a representation artifact: in the column representation the tops are exactly first order (lem:column-representation (3)). The target vanished, which is a supersession found by the work.

The bridge's remedy, a functional-patch gauge glued by Mayer-Vietoris, got its own cycle. entry-2026-09-27-empty-row-sculpting proves 'the functional patch fails': with at most one pigeon, r_i has an empty level set r_i=2, so the patch is never free in direction r_i. Its sculpting replacement was then refuted, and the row-local review shows fall closure reverses the level gap. The first-pass evidence (jordan-type-lead) belongs to the Horace item, but the closure stands on the sculpting entry. The equivalence framing was later replaced by the subset reframing.

entry-2026-09-27-jordan-type-lead shows that a Horace step onto a column is lem:hole-splitting with the terms of conj:fiber-lattice-freeness. On fibers the joint span is the projection of the original one, so 'the step leaves the family as far beyond capacity as before'. The AH/semicontinuity half fails for F_3-rational families (x^3-x). This is a restatement plus an inapplicability, both found by the attempt.

The generic-core review absorbs pinning one row into the confined bases of lem:row-free-subset-sufficiency. The item itself records the many-row break at the per-pigeon rank cap. Pinning lives on in the route as member pinning and pins (A1 status), so the idea is carried forward, not lost.

The three-steps review did real work: an exact pencil-hafnian formula for every coefficient the kill probabilities need. It closed because zeon calculus 'says nothing about the distribution of one fixed coefficient mod 3'. That is inapplicability found by the attempt, and the moment line is off the current route.

The lift review's closure says 'Work this cycle: none needed'. It argues that prop:design-lift-criterion poses the lift without a basis. A reformulation that does not need the basis is not a stronger result that proves the lift, so the supersession claim is unsupported. The lift (N_D cap F_{D-1} contained in N_{D-1}) is again the highest-risk step as conj:lagged-lift-subset, and an IPS-type explicit description of the PC closure is a natural tool for it. The only found obstacle is the functional axioms, an encoding caveat.
next_attempt: Build the analogue of the IPS basis B_d (Definition 2.5, Prop. 2.8) for weak unary PHP without the functional axioms, with its monotonicity x_aQ_i in B_d iff x_a in B_{d-1}. Then test whether it certifies the lagged lift on a restriction set and on the smallest recorded dense family.

reason: The truncated inclusion-exclusion lead was developed over four entries into lem:lucas-truncation and prop:lucas-multiplier-reduction. prop:hiding-needs-emptiness then shows that hiding needs empty deep overlaps, at degree of order n*s. The budget review shows this holds even at the largest range N/2 for pointwise multipliers. This is a falsification of the mechanism, found by the attempt.

Its own test says that it 'is the record's A3 heuristic in the language of the source', and the design-route review confirms it gives no certificate for adversarial forms. A restatement of A3, which is tracked as conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base.

The test itself finds that 'no theorem transfers, since polynomial degree over F_3 is not an information measure'. Its only use is to sharpen the exchange-rate barrier for pointwise multipliers. The colon-multipliers result puts base-design certificates in that class, and that programme is closed. No open statement asks for that barrier.

The bridge's translation is an exact equivalence: an adapted basis is 'the same as a family of commuting idempotent operators'. So beyond its candidate it reformulates distributivity. The candidate 1_{E_b} fails only through the degree filtration, and batched splitting identifies that failure as a fall of the sum of tops, which is the Tor-vanishing statement itself. This is a restatement plus a failed candidate.

The link induction was developed into thm:shared-cell-induction and thm:pair-reduction. It was then made unnecessary by thm:bounded-clusters, which settles the designed case. Link sequences are a Stanley-Reisner cell tool with no translation to non-monomial adversarial forms. Supersession.
Its only aim was the clause count at fixed lambda. Under thm:bounded-clusters lambda may grow to h/(2T), and the explicit column design gives 'every polynomial count, without packings'. Superseded.
The counting of pattern choices served only the levels of the link induction. thm:bounded-clusters' component count replaced that induction. Subsumed.

The support-level coarse-graining was developed and barred by the proved prop:coarse-graining-barrier, which leaves a delta^2 fraction of a dense family in one group. Its coefficient-level form was tracked separately as conj:pseudorandom-taylor. That form was refuted by prop:row-inflation and replaced by conj:column-weight-taylor, so the idea continues there.

The survival review records the bridge as developed into prop:stopping-set-survival: survivor supports are stopping sets of about n^2/(K log_3 n) tops for random families. The part left open, bounding base-class supports, is that line's obstacle itself. The first-pass reason cites the subspace-evasive lead's absorption into prop:relation-avoidance, which belongs to a different item. The closure stands on the stopping-set text.
Developed into prop:stopping-set-survival. The remaining part, 'bounding the supports of base classes, is the route's obstacle above', which makes it a restatement.

Its soundness bound is cor:defect-decay's factor 3, and its derandomization is the spanning condition, both inside prop:relation-avoidance. The survival review found the factor-3 count 'too weak to decide anything by itself'. A restatement.

The split-line review finds that under a split the vectors to avoid have weight at most 2. The null-space property the bridge asks for is then the column-weight condition at t=2, absorbed into prop:split-obstruction-bound, and the open part is the split itself. The first-pass reason (group freeness, Froberg) cites other items. The closure stands on the split-line text.
Same item: the needed null-space property is the column-weight condition at t=2, already in prop:split-obstruction-bound. The open part is the split, so this is a restatement.

The colon-pieces entry developed the lead and found that pieces lie in relative socles. But 'the colon counts cells and cannot show that directions have low weight', and a vanishing colon on small bases is contradicted by the data. That falsifies the lead's target. Inverse systems as a source of designs are a separate item (the budget review's Gorenstein lead).
Its own test reads 'prop:split-obstruction-bound is exactly this statement; it adds no mechanism for the split itself'. The configuration review confirms it. A restatement.

Developed in prop:sequential-freeness, then falsified: its hypothesis 'fails for every single linear relation among three tops' (ex:three-top-relation-types), and the prefix rule cannot avoid planted relations.

Its direct-sum case is the recorded lem:kunneth-component-locality. The tree case went to density evolution, whose girth form the degree-zero circuits refuted, with the content moved into the Mayer-Vietoris and cluster form that the route still carries. Absorbed, not lost.
Developed into prop:square-syzygy-reduction, which proves the defects that the identities give. The taylor-locality review notes that nothing further depends on them.

Tested in local Taylor generation and planted locality, exactly additive on 1544 subfamilies. Its girth form was then refuted by the degree-zero circuits, and its content now lives in the Mayer-Vietoris/cluster form.

One renormalization step was developed into cor:pinned-cluster-reduction, whose stated limit is 'Pinning creates sharing among forms that agree modulo the pins'. The iterated flow is closed by the dense-cover review: 'iterated pinning beyond capacity removes capacity-many forms per round', which is per-block removal with its recorded linear ceiling.
Same bridge. The single step is cor:pinned-cluster-reduction, and the dense-cover review identifies iteration beyond capacity with per-block removal and its recorded linear ceiling.

After several follow-ups, the dependency-line review found that the triangle is generated by its edges and the star by pairs (thm:coordinate-relation-locality). So 'acyclicity of the relation hypergraph is not what locality needs', which falsifies the bridge's prediction.

The predicted ring corrections were found as the covering triples of stars, and chains showed none. The pattern-level mechanism is carried by thm:star-family-locality and thm:adapted-helly-locality, so the bridge has no open question of its own.
The tensor form became thm:involvement-threshold. The proved prop:relation-merging-barrier then shows that tensor superadditivity certifies only a small fraction of the relations beyond capacity.

Developed into thm:adapted-helly-locality. The configuration review falsifies both forms for dense families: shared coordinates give an unbounded Helly number, and span intersections fail since 'the tensor members pairwise meet in 0 and their first-degree dependency needs all (3^{c+1}-1)/2 of them'.
Developed into lem:socle-onset-criterion. The socle question it raised on quotients became, in relation-space form, the Hilbert criterion of prop:relation-merging-barrier. Developed, then superseded.

Developed into the single-relation light cone of lem:relation-space-tor. The proved prop:relation-merging-barrier shows that the light cone certifies only a small fraction of the relations beyond capacity.

Developed into ex:relation-bag-images and thm:coordinate-relation-locality. These show that the triangle, not a tree, is generated by edges, so treewidth is not the governing invariant. Falsification plus a stronger result.

Made exact as prop:first-fall-criterion and run on the tensor family, where the combination does not reduce on the weak base (ex:tensor-family-falls), and on the forced family, where absorption fails for proper-span members. It remains a recorded proved tool.
Used in the transversality criterion: 37 dimensions equal the 3-rank of the line code of PG(2,9). The route no longer depends on relations among squared spans.

It was closed because 'lifting is no longer needed' once the statement moved to satisfiable members. That is a route change, not a reason found against the idea. The current highest-risk step is again a lift (conj:lagged-lift-subset, 'unknown for dense families'). The CN translation, that dense forms map the base onto a grid where every nonzero clause combination is visible, bears on whether dense families' low-degree consequences lift. The record does not say whether it helps or obstructs there.
open_statement: A1 / lagged lift for dense families (conj:lagged-lift-subset)
next_attempt: On the 7-by-6 weak base with six random dense forms, apply the grid-surjectivity + Combinatorial Nullstellensatz argument to decide whether the consequences that the lagged lift must certify by O(D) rows are visible on the base, giving a lift or a counterexample for the smallest tensor family.

reason: The dense-cover review's closure is that 'iterated pinning beyond capacity removes capacity-many forms per round at a robustness cost each time', which is per-block removal with a recorded linear ceiling. That covers the whole flow. The first-pass reason (nerve of the coupled pair) belongs to the nerve item, but the verdict stands on the dense-cover text.

Developed over five reviews: pairs settled by lem:pair-directness-range and prop:overlap-orientation, single directions by end-additivity. The value-side review identifies many-member additivity with its Obstacle, 'cover generation between two halves', so the remainder is a restatement of the open problem.

Developed: flat-covering sunflowers need about (3/2)^k clauses, beyond budget (cor:value-space-dense-covers). Kernel pinning iterated is per-block removal. The coupled-cover review finds that the live obstruction, couplings, 'come from row sums, not from sunflowers'.
The dense-cover review identifies the iterated renormalization flow with per-block removal ('removes capacity-many forms per round at a robustness cost each time'), whose linear ceiling is recorded.

Developed into lem:weak-base-anticoncentration. Below the column-spread scale the image is nearly uniform, and 'beyond it uniformity is impossible', where the obstacle lies. This is a proved limitation, consistent with A1's 'cannot be found by density or spread'.

The member-tensor review closes it because the super dimension is a pointwise, ungraded invariant, and the record has a counterexample that is free pointwise but not free through degree 3. The overdetermined review adds that beyond capacity the allowed ring is not a tensor product of the members' rings, so there is nothing to semisimplify factor by factor. The first-pass evidence (oriented cylinder repair) belongs to another item.
Continued as the generic Jordan type lead, then closed: 'pointwise data cannot certify truncated freeness, by the recorded counterexample'. The graded truncated Dade lemma fails in special position.
Used for the capacities c(b) in prop:oriented-cylinder-repair. The trivial sumset bound suffices, and sharper Kneser bounds do not change which families fail. Its application is exhausted.
Same bridge: the super dimension is pointwise and ungraded, so like rank varieties it cannot see the recorded truncated failures. Beyond capacity there is no tensor factorization to semisimplify.

Total counts factor for the coupled pair and the uncoupled control alike (prop:coupling-distributivity), so product counting does not see couplings. Level-wise counts are the balance test already recorded. Falsified as a detector.
Superseded by prop:ideal-sum-criterion, which gives the obstruction module itself. A Hilbert-function diagnostic 'cannot prove freeness'.

The value-side review finds its general-forms content subsumed by the orbit-weighted moment for random forms, and repeated members falsify it for adversarial families (the ideal-sum review). Both regimes are settled.

The Taylor-route review finds that 'consequences of the clauses alone vanish on the allowed set, so implication chains among clauses are not falls of the row span'. So chain depth does not bear on the lagged lift, which is inapplicability. The lead's test also rested on an unread title result.

Developed in the nontrivial-relation-bound and relation-excess entries: only nontrivial relations absorb, the seed-23 pair has none, and random pairs below the fill point have at most one. Its question is answered, and the answer is carried by A3's relation-excess conditions.

Developed in the junta-residue classes entry: 'row-sum phases carry full top-order mass without any correlation, so the bound is too weak'. It was superseded by the sharper residue-class decomposition.
